---
title: "How the laboratory works"
---

The computational laboratory uses a browser-based working environment so that
all students can use the same scientific software without installing and
configuring Python packages locally.

The working environment has three separate components.

| Component | What it contains | What you do there |
|---|---|---|
| **Course website** | Instructions, assignments, laboratory guides and reference pages | Read the material and follow the laboratory workflow |
| **Personal GitHub workspace** | Notebooks, data, figures, answers and your own results | Work in GitHub Codespaces and save your progress |
| **CluMiner** | Licensed and computationally expensive software | Run CRYSTAL calculations when instructed |

The course website and your workspace are deliberately separate. You should
**not duplicate this website repository**. Instead, you will create your own
private repository from the dedicated Mineral Science workspace template.

## Your personal workspace

Your workspace repository contains two directories with very different roles:

```text
course/
work/
```

`course/` contains material distributed by the teacher. It may be updated
during the course.

`work/` contains **your work**: notebooks, answers, uploaded data, figures and
processed results.

::: {.callout-important}
## One rule prevents most problems

**Do not edit files directly inside `course/`. Work inside `work/`.**
:::

When a new laboratory is released, the usual workflow is:

```text
update-course
      ↓
start-lab NN
      ↓
work/labNN/
      ↓
save → commit → sync
      ↓
stop Codespace
```

You do not need to understand Git internals to use this workflow. The necessary
operations are introduced in the following pages.

## What you need on your own computer

You need:

- a modern web browser;
- a <a href="https://github.com/" target="_blank">GitHub</a> account;
- an internet connection;
- later in the course, an SSH/SFTP client for access to CluMiner.

The Python environment, Jupyter notebooks, and the other scientific tools are
provided inside the Codespace.

Continue with **[Create your personal workspace](02-create-workspace.qmd)**.
